'''Lori Elizabeth Dodd''' is an American [[Mathematical Statistician|mathematical statistician]] specializing in [[clinical trial]]s methodology, statistical analysis of [[Genomics|genomic]] data, design of clinical trials using [[biomarker]]s and imaging modalities, and statistical methods for analyzing biomarkers. She is a statistician in the biostatistics research branch at the [[National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases]].

== Education ==
In 1995, Dodd completed a bachelor's degree in the department of anthropology at the [[University of Utah Honors College]]. Her undergraduate thesis was titled, ''The old people know different: Navajo aging and the aged in the context of change''. Dodd's undergraduate academic advisor was [[Per Hage]], and Charles C. Hughes served as her thesis supervisor.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=The old people know different: Navajo aging and the aged in the context of change|date=1995|language=en|first=Lori Elizabeth|last=Dodd|publisher=University of Utah Honors College|oclc=33130357}}</ref> In 2001, she earned a Ph.D. in the department of biostatistics at the [[University of Washington]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|title=Dodd: Two Topic Imaging Workshop Biosketches|work=[[Radiological Society of North America]]|url=https://www2.rsna.org/re/TwoTopicImagingWorkshopBiosketches/IndexFiles/Dodd.pdf}}</ref> Her dissertation was titled ''Regression methods for areas and partial areas under the receiver-operating characteristic curve''. Dodd's doctoral advisor was [[Margaret Sullivan Pepe]].<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Regression methods for areas and partial areas under the receiver-operating characteristic curve|date=2001|language=en|first=Lori Elizabeth|last=Dodd|publisher=University of Washington|oclc=48806947}}</ref>

== Career ==
Dodd worked at the [[National Cancer Institute]] in the biometric research branch to evaluate [[Imaging biomarker|imaging]] in [[oncology]] trials.<ref name=":0" />

Dodd is a [[Mathematical Statistician|mathematical statistician]] in the division of clinical research's biostatistics research branch at the [[National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases]] (NIAID). She specializes in [[clinical trial]]s methodology, statistical analysis of [[Genomics|genomic]] data, design of clinical trials using [[biomarker]]s and imaging modalities, and statistical methods for analyzing biomarkers.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lori E. Dodd, Ph.D. {{!}} NIH: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases|url=https://www.niaid.nih.gov/about/brb-staff-dodd|website=National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases|date=19 October 2016 |language=en|access-date=2020-05-11}}{{PD-notice}}</ref> At NIAID, she researches the statistical assessment of [[Medical diagnosis|medical diagnostic tests]] and clinical trial design.<ref name=":0" />

In 2016, Dodd conceived of and edited a special issue on [[Ebola]] for the journal ''[[Clinical Trials (journal)|Clinical Trials]]'', which highlighted different approaches to trial design and various viewpoints from the individuals and organizations who contributed to research efforts.<ref>{{Cite web|title=NIH Experts Offer Lessons Learned from the 2014-2015 Ebola Outbreak {{!}} NIH: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases|url=http://www.niaid.nih.gov/news-events/nih-experts-offer-lessons-learned-2014-2015-ebola-outbreak|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917084105/http://www.niaid.nih.gov/news-events/nih-experts-offer-lessons-learned-2014-2015-ebola-outbreak|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 17, 2016|date=January 14, 2016|website=National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases|language=en|access-date=2020-05-11}}{{PD-notice}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Dodd was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]] in 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amstat.org/docs/default-source/amstat-documents/pdfs/fellows/Fellows2024.pdf|title=2024 ASA Fellows|publisher=American Statistical Association|access-date=2024-06-01}}</ref>
